The majority of acetabular components in a cohort of patients undergoing total hip arthroplasty (THA) for osteoporotic acetabular fractures were stable despite the small contact surface achieved between the component and pelvic bone. However, three out of ten patients experienced migration in excess of the limits that predict later loosening in primary THA.

While oversized cups can provide initial stability to some extent, this solution may not be ideal for all patients with osteoporotic acetabular fractures. This is because the small contact surface between the cup and pelvic bone can lead to early loosening and migration. In such cases, other fixation methods, such as screw fixation of the acetabular component or combined hip-sacrum fixation, might be more effective in providing initial stability.

It's essential for clinicians to consider various factors, including patient-specific conditions, fracture anatomy, and treatment goals, when deciding on a surgical approach for osteoporotic acetabular fractures. In some cases, surgeons may need to weigh the benefits of oversized cups against other options and discuss individualized treatment plans with patients.
